newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares rise, institutions dominate bourse.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares rise, institutions dominate bourse.

text.p: Egyptian share prices firmed as institutional investors dominated Sunday's trade, leaving smaller investors thirsting for stocks, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index inched 0.02 points up to 233.93 points with blue-chip cement and milling firms leading the way.
Volume was 177.45 million pounds ($52.19 million), fattened by the listing of shares worth 143.6 million in newly privatised Upper Egypt Flour Mills.

"No one is offering shares, it's very dry. Foreign funds, local funds, companies are holding most of the shares available, leaving individual investors sidelined," said broker Ahmed Hussein of Delta EAB Stockbrokers.

PACHIN/Paints and Chemical Industries was the day's hottest stock, buoyed by a dry market to rise 10.00 pounds and close at 835.00. Heliopolis Housing and Development also gained 9.00 to 105.00 in busy trade.

But it was the favourite milling sector that continued to interest investors, with recently privatised West and Central Delta Flour Mills rising 10.99 pounds to 49.00 during its first day of trade. North Cairo Flour Mills also gained 3.00 pounds to 115.00 in busy trade.
Blue-chip cement firms were slightly lower or unchanged, but Suez Cement rose 0.25 pounds ahead of the National Bank of Egypt's annoucement of its GDR offering on Monday. Shares closed at 52.75.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to a new record high of 363.58 points from Thursday's 358.87 and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 159.94 from 159.91 points.
